discovery: Multiphoton entanglement and satellite-based quantum communication over global distances

nominees.name: Jian-Wei Pan
nominees.affiliation: University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China

motivation: Jian-Wei Pan turned quantum entanglement from a laboratory curiosity into a scalable resource. He pioneered techniques for creating and controlling multiphoton entangled states, showing GHZ-type nonlocality and entanglement swapping, and extending entanglement from three to more than ten photons. He then took these ideas to space. With the Micius satellite (launched 2016) his team distributed entangled photons between ground stations 1,200 km apart, carried out ground-to-satellite quantum teleportation, and ran intercontinental quantum key distribution. These experiments tested quantum mechanics at scales previously out of reach and set up the physical basis of a global quantum network. His work also led to photonic quantum computational advantage. The 2022 prize recognised the foundational Bell tests. Pan's contribution is distinct: he made entanglement a large-scale, engineered quantum resource, from many photons to planetary distances, and in doing so opened the era of practical quantum networks.
